Prevention: When dealing with diseased plants or on diseased land, clean all tools and boots before moving into a clean area.
Avoid repeat cropping of crucifers for at least 6 years, e.g. cauliflower, cabbage, mustard, broccoli, cress, radish.
Instead rotate with non-crucifers such as onion, garlic and legumes.
At least 1 month before seeding, solarise or burn the nursery soil to destroy any disease.
You may need specialist advice on how to do this.
After harvest, collect and burn all plant remnants from the field.
Where possible restrict the movement of water from diseased to healthy areas.
Check the soil pH; acidic soil (below pH 6.5) is favourable for the development of club root.
Raise pH if crucifers are to be grown.

Monitoring: Check whether plants are wilting but also keep a general eye on the growth and development of the plants.
If any plants look suspicious, uproot a few and check the root for club/lumpy shaped growth.
Take action when a minimum of 1 plant has club root infection (irrespective of field size).
Direct Control: Uproot and burn plants with club root.

Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Gloves, mask and overalls required when handling this product.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Despite this it is very toxic and care should be exercised when handling.
